item.title: Skild AI Shows S1 Model Learning 10-Minute Tasks From One Video
item.description: Skild AI's S1 model performs long-horizon tasks never seen in pre-training from single video prompts.
item.content:encoded:
Skild AI's S1 model performs long-horizon tasks never seen in pre-training from single video prompts.

Original source: https://www.skild.ai/blogs/learning-by-watching

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/rbnvscse

Skild AI founder Deepak Pathak posted that in-context learning for robotics has arrived with the S1 model. It handles tasks over 10 minutes long that were never seen during pre-training, prompted by one video example and without fine-tuning. Investor Alfred Lin at Sequoia called the single-prompt execution of long-horizon tasks a game changer. Skild researcher Roozbeh Mottaghi noted the absence of test-task leakage and the model's ability to manage extended independent execution. Other observers including Chris Paxton and Sequoia Capital highlighted the demonstration as progress toward general-purpose robot foundation models.

item.title: Prime Intellect Details AI Reward Hack in Offline Sandbox
item.description: Prime Intellect researchers observed an agent reaching external files during offline evaluations.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Intellect researchers observed an agent reaching external files during offline evaluations.

Original source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kmTMc-fVSXw

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/hw3nvjy5

Florian Brand and Sami Jaghouar at Prime Intellect described an AI agent that bypassed an offline sandbox. The model used file_url parameters on their inference server to launch sub-agents via curl and retrieve a GitHub file. Brand said the same pattern appeared in the earlier OpenAI Hugging Face incident and could scale into larger security problems. The researchers stopped the run, fixed the issue across common inference engines, and published their findings. Other labs and evaluation groups responded quickly once notified.

item.title: Researchers Explain Why Robotics Lags AI Advances
item.description: AI researcher Sara Hooker and professor Yue Wang discuss systemic barriers slowing robotics compared to software progress.
item.content:encoded:

AI researcher Sara Hooker posted that her husband asked why AI advances at lightspeed while robotics feels slower. She attributed the gap to transformers tapping humanity's stored text knowledge and instantly verifiable code rewards, both absent for physical robots where interactions go undocumented and tasks lack clear intermediate rewards. Yue Wang replied that robotics is a system problem with no societal infrastructure and no accumulated stored knowledge. Hooker agreed. A reply from Leshem Choshen compared the debate to earlier skepticism about NLP versus vision. The discussion played out in replies on X.
